papers.version_note: A web page capture (HTML text layer, 2026 footer), not a paper. It has no page breaks, so it is counted as 1 page. The tables for simulator per-minute rates, Hybrid Jobs instances and ML storage hold unrendered template placeholders.
papers.not_read: The simulator per-minute rate table, the Hybrid Jobs instance price tables (standard, compute optimized, accelerated) and the ML storage price are template placeholders in the text layer, so their prices were lost.
papers.what_it_is: Amazon Web Services' public price page for Amazon Braket (QPU, simulator, Hybrid Jobs and notebook pricing, with worked examples).

assertions.value: The page states that Amazon Braket has no upfront charges and that users pay only for the AWS resources they use.
quotes: With Amazon Braket, there are no upfront charges, and you pay only for the AWS resources you use.

assertions.value: The page states that on-demand QPU use has a per-shot fee and a per-task fee, or alternatively a single hourly reservation fee.
quotes: Amazon Braket offers three pricing components for on-demand use of a quantum computer (QPU): a per-shot fee and a per-task fee or a single hourly reservation fee.

assertions.value: The page defines a shot as a single execution of a quantum algorithm on a QPU and a task as a sequence of repeated shots based on the same circuit design or Hamiltonian, with the shot count set when the task is submitted.
quotes: A shot is a single execution of a quantum algorithm on a QPU
A task is a sequence of repeated shots based on the same circuit design or Hamiltonian, with the number of shots defined when you submit the task.
assertions.reader_inference: Definitions as used for billing by the vendor; they set the unit for every QPU price on the page.

assertions.value: The page names gate-based QPUs from AQT, IonQ, IQM and Rigetti, and describes a shot on QuEra's QPU as the time evolution of a Hamiltonian.
quotes: a single pass through a complete quantum circuit on gate-based QPUs from AQT , IonQ , IQM , or Rigetti , or the time evolution of a Hamiltonian on QuEra 's QPU

assertions.value: The page states that per-task pricing is consistent across all QPUs, that per-shot pricing varies by QPU type, and that for gate-based QPUs the per-shot price does not depend on the number or type of gates in the circuit.
quotes: Per-task pricing is consistent across all QPUs, while per-shot pricing varies by QPU type.
For gate-based QPUs, the per-shot price remains the same regardless of the number or type of gates used in a quantum circuit.

assertions.value: The page states that IonQ QPUs require a minimum of 2,500 shots per task when error mitigation is used.
quotes: Note that IonQ QPUs require a minimum of 2,500 shots per task when using error mitigation.

assertions.value: The page's on-demand table lists a per-task price of $0.30000 for every listed QPU, and per-shot prices of $0.02350 (AQT IBEX-Q1), $0.08000 (IonQ Forte), $0.00160 (IQM Emerald), $0.00145 (IQM Garnet), $0.01000 (QuEra Aquila) and $0.000425 (Rigetti Cepheus).
assertions.anchor: Quantum Computers table, Hardware Provider / QPU family / Per-task price / Per-shot price
assertions.reader_inference: Vendor list prices as captured in this page text; a price is a snapshot, so the record must carry the capture date (page footer 2026).

assertions.value: The page's Reservation Mode table lists hourly reservation rates of $4,800.00 (AQT IBEX-Q1), $7,000.00 (IonQ Forte), $4,000.00 (IQM Emerald), $3,000.00 (IQM Garnet), $2,500.00 (QuEra Aquila) and $4,100.00 (Rigetti Cepheus).
quotes: AQT IBEX-Q1 $4,800.00 IonQ Forte $7,000.00 IQM Emerald $4,000.00 IQM Garnet $3,000.00 QuEra Aquila $2,500.00 Rigetti Cepheus $4,100.00

assertions.value: The page states that Braket Direct reserved access is priced by reservation duration rather than task volume, in 1-hour increments, with free cancellation up to 48 hours in advance, and that the hourly reservation fee applies to the actual time booked.
assertions.anchor: Quantum Computers section, Braket Direct Program
quotes: The hourly reservation fee applies to the actual time you book to use a QPU.
Reserved access is priced based on reservation duration rather than task volume, available in 1-hour increments, with free cancellation up to 48 hours in advance.

assertions.value: The page states that Braket Direct expert advice offerings are billed separately from Braket and that experimental capabilities are available on a per-request basis.
assertions.anchor: Quantum Computers section, Braket Direct Program
quotes: Expert advice offerings (billed separately from Braket)
Experimental capabilities (available on a per-request basis)

assertions.value: The page lists a free local simulator in the Braket SDK and three fully managed on-demand simulators, SV1, DM1 and TN1, and describes SV1 as general purpose, DM1 as simulating the effect of noise, and TN1 as specializing in larger scale simulations for certain types of circuits.
quotes: the free local simulator in the Amazon Braket SDK, and three fully managed on-demand simulators: State Vector 1 (SV1), Density Matrix 1 (DM1), and Tensor Network 1 (TN1)

SV1 is a general purpose quantum circuit simulator, DM1 enables you to simulate the effect of noise on your circuits, and TN1 specializes in larger scale simulations for certain types of quantum circuits.

assertions.value: The page states that on-demand simulators are billed at a per-minute rate in increments of one millisecond for the time a simulation runs, with a minimum billing duration of 3 seconds per simulation.
quotes: you are billed at a per-minute rate, in increments of one millisecond, for the time your simulation takes to run, with a minimum billing duration of 3 seconds per simulation

assertions.value: The page states that SV1 and DM1 are available only in US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon) and Europe (London), and that TN1 is available only in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon) and Europe (London).
quotes: on-demand simulators SV1, and DM1, are only available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (N. California), US West (Oregon), and Europe (London).
TN1 is only available in US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), and Europe (London).

assertions.value: The page states that embedded simulators are available only with Braket Hybrid Jobs and are not charged for separately; their cost forms part of the hybrid jobs instance bill.
quotes: The cost for using embedded simulators forms part of your overall bill for using the hybrid jobs instance and is not charged for separately.
Embedded simulators are only available with Amazon Braket Hybrid Jobs.

assertions.value: The page states that Hybrid Jobs supports embedded simulators from PennyLane, such as lightning.qubit and lightning.gpu, and the NVIDIA CUDA-Q framework, and a bring-your-own-container option.
quotes: Amazon Braket Hybrid Jobs supports high-performance embedded simulators from PennyLane, such as the lightning.qubit and lightning.gpu simulator, and using NVIDIA's CUDA-Q framework

assertions.value: The page states that Hybrid Jobs pricing has two components, charges for classical resources and charges for quantum computers or simulators, and that the default instance type is ml.m5.xlarge.
quotes: There are two components to pricing for the Hybrid Jobs feature: charges for the use of classical resources, and charges for the use of quantum computers or quantum simulators.
The Hybrid Jobs feature uses the ml.m5.xlarge instance as the default instance type

assertions.value: The page states that jobs submitted during a reservation have no additional charges beyond the hourly reservation rates, and that quantum task pricing is the same inside or outside a Hybrid Job.
quotes: For jobs submitted during a reservation, there are no additional charges outside of the hourly reservation rates
Pricing for these tasks is the same whether they are run as part of a Hybrid Job or not.

assertions.value: The page states that managed notebooks are hosted and billed by Amazon SageMaker, billed per hour by instance type, with usage under one hour prorated.
quotes: it will be hosted and billed by Amazon SageMaker, the AWS machine learning service
For usage under one hour, cost is prorated based on the hourly price.

assertions.value: The page states that the AWS Free Tier provides one hour of included on-demand simulation time per month for the first twelve months of using Amazon Braket.
quotes: which provides one hour of included on-demand simulation time per month for the first twelve months of using Amazon Braket

assertions.value: The page works an example of a 30-qubit circuit on SV1 at $0.075 per minute for 4 minutes: $0 within the first 12 months, and $0.30 after twelve months.
quotes: design a quantum circuit to use 30 qubits
($0.075 / minute) x 4 minutes =$0.30
Total charges for first 12 months: $0

assertions.value: The page works an example of one task of 10,000 shots on Rigetti Cepheus: a task charge of $0.30, shot charges of $4.25 at $0.000425 per shot, and total charges of $4.55.
quotes: Task charges: 1 task x $0.30 / task = $0.30
Shots charges: 10,000 shots x $0.000425 / shot = $4.25
Total charges: $4.55

assertions.value: The page works an example of a hybrid job on SV1 at $0.075 per minute for 1500 seconds, with an ml.m5.xlarge instance at $0.23 per hour: SV1 charges of $1.875, instance charges of $0.096, total $1.97.
quotes: Total charges: $1.97

assertions.value: The page's Example 4 states a per-shot price of $0.00090 in its description but uses $0.000425 per shot in its calculation, giving task charges of $30.00, shot charges of $4.25, instance charges of $6.36 and total charges of $40.61.
quotes: Task charges: 50 iterations x 2 tasks x $0.30 / task = $30.00
plus each run of the 100 shots at a per-shot price of $0.00090
Shots charges: 50 iterations x 2 tasks x 100 shots x $0.000425 / shot = $4.25
ml.p3.8xlarge usage charges: ($14.688 / 60 minutes) x 26 minutes = $6.36
Total charges: $40.61
assertions.reader_inference: The two per-shot figures disagree inside the same example. The calculation uses the Rigetti Cepheus rate in the price table, so $0.00090 looks like a stale figure in the prose; this is the reader's inference, not the page's statement.

assertions.value: The page works an example of a 24-qubit hybrid job on the embedded lightning.gpu simulator with an ml.p3.8xlarge instance at $0.2448 per minute for 2 minutes: total charges $0.49, with no quantum task charge.
quotes: algorithm on 24 qubits and runs it on the embedded lightning.gpu simulator
ml.p3.8xlarge job instance usage charges: ($0.2448 per-minute) x (2 minutes) = $0.49
Total charges: $0.49

assertions.value: The page works an example of a task with error mitigation and 2,500 shots on IonQ Forte: a $0.30 task charge, $200 shot charges at $0.08 per shot, total $200.30. A task with fewer shots would fail and the scientist would not be charged.
quotes: Task charges: 1 task x $0.30 / task = $0.30
Shots charges: 2,500 shots x $0.08 / shot = $200
Total charges: $200.30
attempting to run such a task with fewer shots will fail and the scientists would not be charged

assertions.value: The page footer carries a 2026 copyright notice; the prices on the page are the vendor's list prices as captured in this text, and the page text does not carry its own price-effective date.
quotes: © 2026, Amazon Web Services, Inc. or its affiliates. All rights reserved.
assertions.certainty_reason: The footer settles the year of the page capture; the page states no effective date for the prices.
assertions.reader_inference: Any price taken from this page is a snapshot and should be stored with its capture date, not as a durable fact.

assertions.value: The page text carries unrendered template placeholders such as {regionSelector} and {bulkPriceOf!...} in place of the simulator per-minute rates, the Hybrid Jobs instance prices and the ML storage price.
quotes: Quantum Circuit Simulators {regionSelector} Simulator  Per-minute rate
assertions.certainty_reason: The placeholders appear verbatim in the text layer; only prices quoted in the worked examples survive (SV1 at $0.075 per minute).
assertions.reader_inference: Simulator, instance and storage prices cannot be taken from this record except where an example quotes them.
